foundations.geology: Kings Heath B14 sits on the Mercia Mudstone Group (Triassic), SE of the Birmingham Fault: mudstones up to ~300m thick, weathering at surface to firm/stiff reddish-brown silty CLAY (Grade IVa/IVb) over progressively less-weathered mudstone. Critically for this job, BGS/engineering-geology data (NORA RR/01/02; Lyell Collection 2024 3D VCP study) give the MMG an upper-quartile modified plasticity index indicative of LOW volume-change potential - some weathered/silty horizons even fall below the 10% modified-PI threshold and are NOT classed as shrinkable at all. Contrast London/Gault Clay (high VCP). So the default working assumption for 115 Vicarage Road is LOW shrinkability, possibly non-shrinkable, but MMG is variable (weaker material can underlie stronger; local plasticity spikes occur), which is exactly what the GBP 1,500 borehole + Atterberg limits (modified PI = PI x fraction passing 425um) must confirm. NHBC bands: modified PI >=40% = high VCP, 20-40% = medium, 10-20% = low, <10% = not shrinkable (tree tables do not apply). The borehole should also prove depth to competent mudstone (typically shallow here), which sets pile/pad bearing if needed.
foundations.nhbc_depths: REGIME A - NHBC Chapter 4.2 (soil shrinkage) is what actually sets foundation DEPTH, enforced via Building Regs/insurer, not the RPA. Method: (1) classify soil VCP from modified PI; (2) classify tree water demand by species - HIGH: oak, willow, poplar, elm, eucalyptus, hawthorn, cypresses; MODERATE: ash(NHBC lists as moderate-high in older eds - verify), sycamore, beech, lime, cherry, horse chestnut, apple, plane; LOW: birch, hornbeam, holly, elder, magnolia, hazel; (3) take D = trunk centre to nearest foundation face (~6.0m to the new rear wall here; returns 6-12m), H = species MATURE height (not current height); (4) read depth from the 4.2 charts/tables (Tables 11-19 in older editions) for the D/H ratio; trench fill deeper than 2.5m needs engineer design (TR R5). Minimum depths in shrinkable clay even with no tree: 1.0m (high VCP), 0.9m (medium), 0.75m (low). WORKED DEPTHS for the rear wall at D=6m (approximate chart readings - engineer to confirm from current NHBC 4.2): IF OAK (high demand, H=20m, D/H=0.30): low-shrink soil ~1.5-1.6m; medium ~1.9-2.1m; high ~2.3-2.5m. IF WILLOW/POPLAR (high demand, H=24-28m, D/H=0.21-0.25): low ~1.7-1.9m; medium ~2.2-2.4m. IF MODERATE species (e.g. sycamore/beech, H~20-22m, D/H~0.27-0.30): low ~1.2-1.4m; medium ~1.5-1.8m. IF LOW demand (birch, H=14m, D/H=0.43): low ~0.75-1.0m (i.e. barely above minimum); medium ~1.0-1.2m. IF modified PI <10% (real possibility on MMG): soil not shrinkable, tree irrelevant to depth, standard ~0.75-1.0m strip/trench to competent stratum. Punchline: on LOW-shrink Mercia Mudstone a 700mm-trunk tree at 6m deepens a trench-fill by roughly 0.5-0.9m at worst (high-demand species) - it does NOT force piles. Depths taper along the returns as D grows; only the rear ~10-12m needs the full depth, the front of the flanks can step back toward 0.9-1.0m. Crown reduction: NHBC gives NO credit - design on species mature height because regrowth (a few seasons) and future management cannot be guaranteed; pruning does not reduce required depth.
foundations.rpa_regime: REGIME B - BS 5837:2012 RPA is an ARBORICULTURAL/planning construct, not a foundation-depth rule. RPA = area of a circle radius 12 x stem diameter (0.7m x 12 = 8.4m, ~707 m2 cap), a nominal zone where digging/compaction should by default be avoided to keep a RETAINED tree viable. It binds you only through (a) planning conditions/validation - Birmingham, like most LPAs, expects BS 5837 information (tree survey/AIA, sometimes AMS + tree protection plan) on householder applications where a mature tree stands within ~12m of the works, and can condition tree protection; and (b) TPO/conservation-area law if the tree is protected (Kings Heath: no conservation area; TPO unknown - check first). Building control and NHBC do not enforce the RPA. Crucially, BS 5837 para 7.4 itself contemplates construction WITHIN the RPA where justified by a project arboriculturist: hand-dug or air-spade trial trenches to map actual roots, root-sensitive excavation under arb supervision, retained root pruning protocols, and only local engineering solutions (pile/beam, cantilever) where significant roots are actually found. Note the structural root zone of a 700mm stem is only ~2.8-4m; at 6m+ you are in the outer RPA where major roots are sparse. So: an AMS + trial-trench route is a lawful, recognised and normally cheaper alternative to blanket screw piles for a householder extension - Birmingham can only insist on no-dig within the RPA via an explicit condition (typically where the tree is TPO'd or of high amenity value), and even then the AMS route is the standard mechanism to discharge it. The current bill's assumption that RPA-clip = must-pile conflates the two regimes.
options_costed: OPTION 1 - Deep trench-fill + Claymaster + slip membrane, 29m run, 600mm wide, GEN1 via volumetric mixer (~GBP 115-130/m3, pay-for-what-you-pour), dig+grab-away (~GBP 190-300/8t load, soil ~1.8t/m3 bulked x1.3): at 1.5m: dig 26m3 (7 loads ~GBP 1,900), concrete ~23.5m3 ~GBP 2,900, digger+driver 3-4 days ~GBP 1,300, Claymaster 50mm tree-side face ~23m2 ~GBP 350 + membrane/sundries ~GBP 250 = ~GBP 6,700-8,000. At 2.0m: dig 35m3 (~GBP 2,600), concrete ~32m3 ~GBP 4,000, trench boxes/shoring ~GBP 1,000, plant 5 days ~GBP 1,600, heave kit ~GBP 500 = ~GBP 9,700-11,500. At 2.5m: dig 43.5m3 (~GBP 3,300), concrete ~41m3 ~GBP 5,100, serious shoring ~GBP 2,000, plant ~GBP 2,000, heave kit + engineer cert = ~GBP 13,000-15,500 (at this depth piles compete and safety/insurance risk rises - avoid).

OPTION 2 - Screw piles + RC ground beams as billed: GBP 18,000, value-engineered GBP 14,250. Market check 2026: screw piling GBP 100-200/lm, extension piling projects GBP 8,000-18,000; for ~16-18 piles + 29m beams the VE figure is plausible but top-of-market. Fast, no muck-away, arb-friendly - but only buys anything if the LPA actually conditions no-dig or the borehole comes back medium-shrink with a high-demand species.

OPTION 3 - Augered/sectional-flight mini-piles + ground beams: ~16-18 piles x 6m = ~100-110 lm at GBP 75-150/lm = GBP 8,000-16,000 incl. mobilisation GBP 2,500-3,500, plus 29m RC ground beam GBP 3,200-4,600: realistic all-in GBP 12,000-16,000. Rarely beats screw piles at this scale; spoil from augers is an RPA negative.

OPTION 4 - Pad-and-beam: ~11 pads at 2.5-2.75m centres dug to design depth (2.0-2.5m) + reinforced ground beams spanning: GBP 800-1,200/pad + beams = ~GBP 9,500-13,000. Less concrete and muck than deep trench at 2.5m, but pads still excavate within the RPA (needs same arb cover) and needs engineer design - a niche middle option.

OPTION 5 - Hybrid as current plan, shrunk: the 8.4m RPA arc from a tree 6m behind the rear wall clips roughly the rear 8.6m wall + ~1.5-2m of each return, i.e. ~10-12m of the 29m. Pile only that strip (~8 screw piles + beam ~GBP 6,000-7,500) + trench-fill the remaining ~17-19m at 1.5m (~GBP 4,000-4,700) = GBP 10,500-12,500. YES it can shrink further: (a) depth on the piled strip is a planning/arb question not an NHBC one, so if the TPO check is clear or the AMS trial-trench route is agreed, convert the strip to trench-fill too (whole job Option 1 at ~GBP 7,000-9,000 + arb fees GBP 600-1,200); (b) even if piling stays, re-tender it - 8 screw piles + one beam should not carry GBP 14,250 of value.
foundations.tree_verdict: FIRST ACTIONS (cheap, this week): (1) TPO check - Birmingham City Council publishes TPO locations on its GIS mapping system and a 'Find out if a tree is protected' page (birmingham.gov.uk/info/20184); cross-check tposearch.co.uk for B14 7QG and confirm in writing with the planning duty/tree officer (data.gov.uk dataset exists but council warns it may lag - written confirmation is the insurable evidence). Kings Heath has no conservation area, so if no TPO the tree is legally unprotected. (2) Species ID from a photo/arborist visit - this single fact swings the design depth by ~0.6-0.9m (oak/willow/poplar = high water demand vs birch/hornbeam = low) and is free. FELL-VS-DESIGN HONESTLY: felling a ~700mm-stem, ~18-20m tree costs GBP 1,000-2,500 (large/complex up to GBP 3,000) + stump grind GBP 150-500 = ~GBP 1,200-3,000 all-in 2026. But NHBC 4.2 also governs foundations near REMOVED trees: on medium/high-shrink clay the desiccated soil rehydrates over years-to-decades and heaves, so you must either design for the tree as if still present or add full heave precautions (deeper trench + compressible fill + suspended floors) - felling is NOT a clean win there. On LOW-shrink soil the recoverable deficit is small, so felling genuinely would drop you to ~1.0-1.2m trench (~GBP 6,000-7,500) - but that totals GBP 7,500-10,500 with the felling, i.e. roughly cost-neutral against simply designing around the tree at 1.5m (GBP 7,000-9,000), while permanently losing garden screening, risking a provisional/emergency TPO if the council gets wind mid-application (felling an unprotected tree is lawful, but a live application puts the tree on officers' radar and sours the case file), and burning neighbour goodwill on a party-flank build that needs their cooperation. CROWN REDUCTION: no help - NHBC gives zero foundation credit for pruning because regrowth restores water demand and management cannot be secured. VERDICT: keep the tree, confirm no TPO, ID the species, and design to NHBC 4.2 depths with an AMS/trial-trench route instead of blanket piles. Fell only if species ID says willow/poplar/oak AND the borehole says medium-shrink AND the LPA raises no objection - and even then price the heave precautions before assuming a saving.
scenario_costs: S1 - Borehole: modified PI <10% (non-shrinkable weathered mudstone at founding level), any species: standard trench-fill 0.75-1.0m to competent stratum, tree irrelevant to depth; AMS + hand-dig within RPA arc: foundation line ~GBP 5,500-7,000 (saves ~GBP 7,500+ vs VE'd bill).
S2 - Low VCP (PI 10-20%) + moderate/low-demand species: trench-fill 1.2-1.4m + Claymaster tree side: ~GBP 6,500-8,000.
S3 - Low VCP + high-demand species (oak/willow/poplar): trench-fill 1.5-1.9m stepped (full depth rear 12m only) + Claymaster + slip membrane + AMS: ~GBP 7,500-9,500.

S4 - Medium VCP (PI 20-40%) + high-demand species: 2.0-2.4m trench with shoring (~GBP 10,500-13,000) vs hybrid pile-the-rear-strip + 1.5m elsewhere (~GBP 10,500-12,500) vs full VE'd screw piles GBP 14,250 - take the hybrid, re-tendered: ~GBP 11,000-12,500.
S5 - Tree TPO'd or LPA conditions no-dig in RPA: hybrid piled strip + trench-fill remainder ~GBP 11,000-13,000; blanket screw piles GBP 14,250 is the ceiling, not the plan.
S6 - Fell (only if confirmed unprotected), low-shrink borehole: felling+stump GBP 1,200-3,000 + 1.0-1.2m trench GBP 6,000-7,500 = GBP 7,500-10,500 total - no better than S2/S3, so not recommended.

In every scenario keep the GBP 1,500 borehole - it is the cheapest lever on the whole line: expected saving vs the GBP 14,250 VE'd bill is GBP 2,000-8,500 depending on scenario, most likely landing the foundation line at GBP 7,500-9,500.

price_table: 100mm DENSE 7.3N common (17-19kg): materials GBP 1.10-1.50/block trade bulk Midlands (Wickes single retail GBP 2.70; Checkatrade 2026 guide GBP 0.95-1.40; 2Brothers GBP 1.65-2.10) = GBP 11-15/m2 at 10/m2 + mortar/ties GBP 2.50/m2; price-work labour GBP 18-22/m2 (two-handed but routine). Supply+lay ~GBP 33-37/m2. CHEAPEST structural leaf. Lambda ~1.13 - useless thermally.

100mm MEDIUM-DENSE 3.6-7.3N (13-15kg): GBP 1.40-1.90/block = GBP 14-19/m2 materials; labour GBP 17-20/m2. Supply+lay ~GBP 36-39/m2. Lambda ~0.45-0.60 - still not enough for the 0.18 cavity alone. Pays for itself only where a gang discounts for the lighter block; usually GBP 2-4/m2 dearer than dense for no compliance gain on a rendered outer leaf.

100mm STANDARD AIRCRETE 3.6N (Thermalite Shield/Celcon Standard, ~8.5kg, lambda 0.15): GBP 1.90-2.40/block trade (Wickes single GBP 2.55) = GBP 19-24/m2; labour GBP 15-18/m2 (one-hand lift, fastest conventional laying). Supply+lay ~GBP 37-42/m2. REQUIRED on the inner leaf: with 150mm full-fill lambda 0.032, dense inner gives U~0.19-0.20 (fail vs 0.18); aircrete inner lambda 0.15 gives U~0.17 (pass). 3.6N is adequate for 2-storey+attic-truss loading subject to SE check; use padstones/hard spots at beam bearings instead of upgrading the whole leaf.

100mm HIGH-STRENGTH AIRCRETE 7.3N (~11kg, lambda 0.19): GBP 2.40-3.00/block = GBP 24-30/m2; labour GBP 16-18/m2. Supply+lay ~GBP 43-48/m2. GBP 5-7/m2 dearer than standard aircrete AND worse lambda - specify only as spot blocks under bearings, never wholesale.

LARGE-FORMAT AIRCRETE - Celcon Plus 440x430 (0.19m2/block, ~5.3/m2) and Jumbo Blok 630x250 thin-joint (~6.3/m2): materials roughly GBP 21-26/m2 + Celfix thin-joint mortar GBP 2-3/m2. Labour CAN fall to GBP 12-15/m2 at 40-45m2/day with a practised thin-joint gang (Advanced New Builds claims 3x output), but typical Midlands domestic gangs do not price-work thin-joint cheaper - most quote the same or add for unfamiliarity, first-course levelling and special tooling. On a 200m2 job the theoretical GBP 3-5/m2 saving usually evaporates. Only take it if a gang quotes it lower in writing.

140mm VARIANTS: 140mm dense 7.3N (24-25kg) GBP 1.90-2.60/block = GBP 19-26/m2 materials BUT exceeds the HSE 20kg repetitive-handling threshold - two-person or mechanical handling mandated (HSE blocks/masonry guidance, Lignacite guide), price-work jumps to GBP 25-32/m2 and gangs resist. 140mm aircrete (~12kg) GBP 2.60-3.30/block = GBP 26-33/m2, labour normal. Neither is needed in this spec - avoid 140mm dense anywhere manual. CHEAPEST LEAF COMBO: outer (rendered) 100mm dense 7.3N common ~GBP 34/m2 supply+lay (dense also takes render with less shrinkage-crack risk than aircrete, which needs basecoat+mesh); inner (drylined) 100mm standard aircrete 3.6N ~GBP 39/m2 (Part L necessity, not luxury). ~200m2 total = ~GBP 7,300-7,800 supply-and-lay.
blocks.below_dpc: Over the ~29m perimeter, only the non-RPA runs (roughly 18-22m once the piled/ground-beam RPA zone is netted off) are in play; the beam zone has no below-DPC blockwork question. Three options at 0.6-1.0m below DPC (say 0.75m average): (1) TRENCH/FOUNDATION BLOCKS 300mm wide, one block replacing both skins - dense aggregate trench 440x215x300 GBP 4.50-6.00/block trade (Mannok Lite foundation GBP 5.40 listed; aircrete Celcon trench GBP 8.96-11.52 trade - avoid, twice the money for no benefit below ground); ~8 blocks/lm at 3.5 courses = GBP 36-48/lm materials + GBP 15-20/lm laying = GBP 51-68/lm. No cavity, no ties, no weak-mix cavity fill, fast. (2) CAVITY-TO-GROUND (two 100mm dense skins + ties + lean-mix cavity fill below ground): ~GBP 20-24/lm blocks + GBP 8-10 fill/ties + GBP 25-30 labour = GBP 55-70/lm, slowest and most defect-prone - reject. (3) POURED CONCRETE HIGH (raise the trench-fill pour to ~2 courses below DPC): extra concrete at GBP 110-130/m3 2026 = ~GBP 45-55/lm for a 600mm trench, near-zero labour since it is part of the pour (trench-fill benchmark GBP 170-280/lm total, costestimator.co.uk). VERDICT: on Mercia Mudstone firm strata, pour the trench-fill concrete high and finish with two courses of 300mm dense trench block to DPC - cheapest and fastest combination, ~GBP 10-20/lm below the cavity-to-ground detail = GBP 200-450 saved on ~20m, and it removes a trade visit. Do NOT use aircrete trench blocks (freeze-thaw fine but double the price); dense 7.3N trench blocks carry the sulfate/DS class check for Mercia Mudstone groundwater - confirm ACEC class from the GBP 1,500 borehole before final concrete/block spec.
blocks.productivity: Real 2026 numbers: sand-and-cement blockwork runs 150-200 blocks/day per layer = 15-20m2/day (Build It / trade forums); dense 100mm solid (17-19kg, two-handed every lift) sits at the bottom, 130-180/day; standard aircrete (8.5kg, genuinely one-handed) sits at the top, 180-220/day - so yes, aircrete's weight advantage is real and shows up as roughly +15-25% output and GBP 2-4/m2 off the price-work rate. 2026 Midlands price-work for 100mm blockwork is GBP 17.50-20/m2 (Green's Brickwork cost guide; general bricklayer day rate GBP 200-300); expect ~GBP 16-18/m2 quoted for aircrete, GBP 18-22/m2 for dense. Thin-joint large-format claims 40-45m2/day (Advanced New Builds) and storey-height in a day because Celfix sets in 10-20 minutes, but only specialist gangs hit it - ordinary domestic gangs will not discount for it. 140mm dense at 24-25kg breaches the HSE 20kg repetitive-handling guidance (HSE construction manual-handling pages; Lignacite guide): mandated two-person or mechanical handling roughly halves effective output and pushes rates to GBP 25-32/m2 - it genuinely kills the rate; nothing in this design needs it. PM lever: let the gang price the two leaves separately - a blended single rate always drifts to the dense rate.
blocks.seconds_channels: Live Birmingham channels, August 2026: Gumtree Birmingham bricks/blocks category - surplus blocks at GBP 1 each negotiable on quantity, leftover part-packs at GBP 40/pallet (vs GBP 130-180 new), reclaimed imperial bricks 75p in Yardley; Facebook Marketplace Birmingham has an active bricks-and-cinder-blocks category; SurplusBuilder.com is a dedicated UK trade-clearance marketplace for overstock; plus part-load dealers and merchant yard clearances (ask E H Smith, Lords, Selco Birmingham branches for banded end-of-run packs). Realistic saving 30-60% on the outer-leaf dense commons = GBP 400-900 on this job's ~1,000 outer blocks. THE CERTIFICATION CATCH: structural masonry must have a declared compressive strength with a UKCA/CE Declaration of Performance to BS EN 771-3 (aggregate) or 771-4 (aircrete). The DoP travels with the product, not the invoice - so NEW-BUT-SURPLUS blocks in original banded packs with legible pack labels are fully acceptable to SE and Building Control: photograph and keep every pack label. Loose, unbanded, weathered or unknown-brand lots have no traceable declared strength; BC can refuse them for the superstructure and independent testing to BS EN 772-1 (the route the Reclaimed Brick Company used for bricks) costs more than the saving on a 200m2 job. Factory seconds sold by the maker as cosmetic seconds usually retain the DoP - fine behind render/drylining. Rule: full labelled packs of a known brand only; never loose lots for anything load-bearing.
blocks.exotics: KILL 215mm hollow + rebar + site fill (US CMU style): blocks GBP 4.00-5.50 each (~GBP 40-55/m2 materials, 2Brothers/Checkatrade 2026), plus rebar, plus C20 infill and pump/pokering, plus you lose the cavity so hitting U 0.18 forces external insulation under the render (EWS buildup ~GBP 60-90/m2) or internal insulation losing floor area - total wall cost well above the GBP 34-39/m2 cavity leaves, and a non-standard single-skin house wall invites SE fees, BC queries and mortgage-valuer caution. Numbers kill it twice over; it only wins for retaining walls. KILL hollow blocks filled on site as a cheap plain leaf: the fill labour erases the ~GBP 1/block saving. KILL/NEUTRAL recycled-aggregate blocks (Lignacite ECO 50/70, Besblock): fully certified with DoP and EPD so compliance is clean - but they price at parity or a small premium to standard medium-dense, so zero saving; keep only if a local merchant clears them below dense-common money. KILL reclaimed/used blocks for the superstructure (no DoP - see seconds section). Nothing exotic beats a dense 7.3N common at GBP 1.10-1.50; the British block market is too efficient at the bottom.
blocks.verdict_spec: SPEC: Outer leaf (rendered) 100mm dense 7.3N aggregate common to BS EN 771-3, bought as banded surplus/part-load packs where labels survive, ~GBP 34/m2 supply-and-lay (GBP 24-28/m2 if surplus sourcing lands). Inner leaf 100mm STANDARD aircrete 3.6N lambda 0.15 (Thermalite Shield/Celcon Standard) ~GBP 39/m2 - non-negotiable for U 0.18 with 150mm lambda-0.032 full-fill (dense inner = ~0.20 fail; hi-strength aircrete = dearer AND thermally worse); 7.3N aircrete or padstones as spot blocks at beam bearings only, per SE. No 140mm dense anywhere (HSE >20kg = GBP 7-10/m2 labour penalty). Thin-joint large-format only if a gang commits to a lower written rate - do not assume it. BELOW DPC (non-RPA runs, ~20m): pour trench-fill concrete high, finish with two courses 300mm dense 7.3N trench block to DPC; no cavity below ground; sulfate class confirmed by the borehole. MONEY vs the bill: superstructure blockwork at market spec (hi-strength aircrete inner + medium-dense or aircrete outer, blended labour) prices at ~GBP 8,800-9,600 for 200m2; this spec lands ~GBP 7,300-7,800 mainstream-bought = GBP 1,200-2,000 saved, plus GBP 400-900 from surplus-pack sourcing of the outer commons, plus GBP 200-450 on the below-DPC detail = TOTAL GBP 1,800-3,300 saved against the 14.3k VE'd package's blockwork + trench share, with labour rates held at GBP 16-20/m2 by keeping every unit under 20kg and price-working the leaves separately. Honest ceiling: blocks are a GBP 2-3k lever on this job; the GBP 5k+ lever remains the tree - identify the species and commission the arboricultural RPA check, because a smaller true RPA (or a low-category tree) converts piled beams back to trench-fill, which dwarfs every block decision above. Confidence medium: all prices from published 2026 guides and merchant listings, not written Midlands quotes - firm up with two-merchant pricing on exact quantities before committing.

killed: KILLED: any trench-fill inside the RPA of a RETAINED tree. An open trench 1.0-2.5m deep severs structural roots of a 700mm-stem tree; BS 5837 no-dig applies at planning, the arboriculturist won't sign the method statement, NHBC 4.2 and warranty surveyors bounce it, and a later tree-death/heave claim is uninsured. Inside the RPA of a retained tree it is piles + suspended ground beams or nothing.

KILLED/CORRECTED: treating the BS 5837 RPA (12 x 0.70m = 8.4m radius - the arithmetic itself is correct) as a statutory foundation constraint. RPA is a planning-stage tree-PROTECTION metric. With no conservation area and (if confirmed) no TPO, the owner may lawfully fell their own garden tree (garden trees are exempt from Forestry Act felling licences) or dig near it. What NEVER goes away, TPO or not, is NHBC Chapter 4.2 depth/heave design on shrinkable soil, enforced via building control/SE/warranty. The dossier conflated the two regimes.

KILLED: committing GBP 18,000 (even VE'd to 14,250) of piling before spending GBP 0 on the BCC TPO register check and ~GBP 150-250 on a species/condition ID. Both unknowns are checkable in under a week and one branch deletes most of the pile line.

KILLED: screw piles as the default system without the borehole. Kings Heath is on Mercia Mudstone; if weathered mudstone turns to strong rock at 2-4m, helical piles hit torque refusal. Verified 2026 rates: screw piles GBP 100-200/lm, augered mini-piles GBP 75-180/lm, whole-extension mini-piling packages GBP 4,500-8,000 - so even the piled branch at 14.25k carries fat; sectional-flight augered mini-piles are the fallback and often cheaper.

KILLED: felling a HIGH-water-demand species (oak, willow, poplar, elm) on medium-or-worse shrinkable soil and then trench-filling without heave precautions - moisture recovery heave runs for 10+ years and NHBC 4.2 requires heave protection (compressible board/void formers, deeper toe) or it's a future subsidence-register entry that kills mortgageability. Fell-and-trench-fill is ONLY clean on confirmed LOW volume-change-potential soil.

KILLED (block dossier): the GBP 7,200 blockwork labour line and the VE verdict that it is 'already price-work-lean, hold, risk none'. It contradicts the dossier's OWN quoted rate: 2026 price-work is GBP 17.50-20/m2 for 100mm blockwork (verified); 200m2 x GBP 18.75 = ~GBP 3,750, plus overhand party-flank premium, cavity trays/closers, gable raking and daywork details ~GBP 1,400 = ~GBP 5,150. The line has ~GBP 2,000 of fat at its own rates.

KILLED (block dossier): DriTherm 32 150mm at GBP 1,400 for ~100m2 of cavity (GBP ~13/m2). Verified 2026 price is GBP 21.70-23.40/m2 ex VAT even at pallet quantity - the line is GBP 700-900 UNDER-provided and must be corrected UP to ~GBP 2,200. Do not VE to DriTherm 35/37: with a 100mm lambda-0.15 aircrete inner leaf, 150mm at lambda 0.035 gives U~0.19 and fails the 0.18 extension-wall limit; lambda 0.032 is the floor of the spec.

KILLED: 'seconds' or downgraded blocks in EITHER structural leaf. Structural masonry needs a declared BS EN 771 compressive strength and UKCA/CE declaration of performance for the SE's calcs, building control and any warranty; undeclared seconds fail structural certification. (Seconds PIR in the ground FLOOR is fine and stays - non-structural, branded boards with declared lambda.)

FLAGGED, not killed: Mercia Mudstone locally contains gypsum - the GBP 1,500 borehole MUST include a sulfate suite (BRE SD1 DS/AC class) and Atterberg/plasticity tests, or below-ground concrete and the shrinkability classification are both guesses. Also: if the tree is retained on a planning application, expect BCC to condition an arb method statement; and an LPA can serve an emergency TPO once an application flags a fine tree - so resolve the tree question BEFORE submitting planning.
decision_tree: STEP 0 (this week, ~GBP 200 total): (a) BCC TPO register check - free; (b) arboriculturist species + condition note GBP 150-250; (c) commission the GBP 1,500 borehole NOW with plasticity index + sulfate suite specified. Nothing else on the foundation line is decided until these land.

BRANCH 1 - NO TPO + borehole LOW shrinkability (mod. plasticity index <20% or rock at shallow depth), ANY species: fell and grub the tree (GBP 1,500-2,500 verified for a large mature tree incl. ~GBP 500 stump grind), photograph/record condition first, fell BEFORE the planning submission (lawful - no TPO, no conservation area, garden trees felling-licence exempt). Then plain trench-fill 1.0-1.5m over the full ~24m of new runs at GBP 220-280/lm = GBP 5,300-6,700. FOUNDATION LINE: GBP 7,300-8,700 (say 8,000). Saves ~GBP 6,250 vs 14,250. Heave negligible on low-VCP soil - insurable and mortgageable with the SI report on file.

BRANCH 2 - NO TPO + MEDIUM shrinkability + LOW/moderate water-demand species (e.g. birch, rowan, pine, apple): RETAIN the tree. Deep trench-fill to the NHBC 4.2 species/distance depth (typ. 1.5-2.0m here) on the ~11m of runs outside the RPA at GBP 250-350/lm = GBP 3,000-3,800; pile only the RPA-clipped rear strip (~13m: rear 8.6m wall + last 2.4m of each flank) - 7-8 piles + suspended beam = GBP 8,000-9,000 incl. mobilisation. FOUNDATION LINE: GBP 11,500-12,500. Saves ~GBP 2,250-2,750.

BRANCH 3 - NO TPO + MEDIUM/HIGH shrinkability + HIGH water-demand species (oak/willow/poplar/elm): do NOT fell (heave). Keep the hybrid but VE per the borehole: respace piles to 2.5-3.0m centres on deeper beams, augered mini-piles outside the RPA, screw piles only where the arb requires low-disturbance. FOUNDATION LINE: GBP 12,500-14,000. Saves GBP 250-1,750. (A HIGH-shrinkability result on Mercia Mudstone is itself suspect - re-test before paying for it.)

BRANCH 4 - TPO EXISTS (or BCC flags/TPOs the tree during the application): tree stays; TPO works consent + arb method statement for any RPA incursion (fold into the SI line, ~GBP 400-600); piles + suspended beams in the RPA, NHBC-depth trench-fill outside it, exactly as currently designed. FOUNDATION LINE: GBP 13,500-14,250 (hold). Saves ~GBP 0-750. This is the ONLY branch where the current 14.25k line is the right answer.

ALL BRANCHES: below-ground concrete to the DC/AC class the sulfate suite returns (gypsum risk in Mercia Mudstone); beam-and-block floor line (GBP 5,000) holds in branches 2-4; in branch 1 it may VE to a ground-bearing slab for ~GBP 800-1,000 more saving - SE's call.
verdict.block_spec: RECOMMENDED WALL (hits U<=0.18 - verified arithmetic: Rse 0.04 + render 0.03 + 100mm med-dense outer 0.18-0.20 + DriTherm 32 150mm R=4.69 + 100mm aircrete lambda-0.15 R=0.67 + p'board/dab 0.19 + Rsi 0.13 => U ~ 0.17-0.18): INNER LEAF: 100mm aircrete - ground storey in 7.3N high-strength aircrete (lambda ~0.19, AD-A/SE requirement for the lowest storey of an effectively 3-storey masonry building; U still ~0.179), first floor and attic storey in standard 3.6N aircrete (lambda 0.15), ~GBP 1.85-2.30/block trade (verified GBP 2.28-2.42 retail). OUTER LEAF: 100mm 7.3N MEDIUM-DENSE concrete, ~GBP 1.10-1.50/block - NOT aircrete under render (movement joints at ~3m and bed-joint reinforcement vs 6m on dense; cracking risk on a rendered elevation). CAVITY: 150mm Knauf DriTherm 32 - non-negotiable; lambda 0.035 fails 0.18 with this build-up; corrected line GBP ~2,200 (verified GBP 21.7-23.4/m2 ex VAT). BELOW DPC: 100mm 7.3N dense concrete both leaves, cavity filled with lean-mix to ground level, mix to the sulfate class from the SI (gypsum in Mercia Mudstone). NO seconds/undeclared blocks anywhere structural; seconds PIR stays in the floor only. MONEY vs the 14.3k line: labour 7,200 -> 5,150 (its own GBP 17.50-20/m2 price-work rate x 200m2 + GBP 1,400 dayworks/overhand flank premium); blocks 4,500 -> 3,600 (mixed spec above at trade prices); DriTherm 1,400 -> 2,200 (UP - was under-provided); ties/DPC/mortar 1,200 hold. NEW BLOCKWORK LINE: ~GBP 12,150. NET SAVING: ~GBP 2,150 (firm, not condition-dependent - and honest, because it nets off the 800 insulation under-pricing the old line was hiding).

FOUNDATIONS are branch-dependent: best branch (no TPO + low-shrink Mercia Mudstone, ~45% likely on this geology) saves ~GBP 6,250; hybrid branch ~GBP 2,500; TPO/high-demand hold branch ~GBP 0-750; probability-weighted expectation ~GBP 3,800-4,000. REALISTIC COMBINED SAVING: ~GBP 6,000 central (band GBP 2,900 worst-branch to GBP 9,300 best-branch, including a possible +GBP 900 slab swap in branch 1). NEW PROJECT TOTAL off the ~GBP 176k base: ~GBP 170k central; ~GBP 166.5-167k if the borehole and TPO check both break your way; ~GBP 173k if the tree is protected and the clay is worse than the geology says. Sequencing is the whole game: the GBP ~200 TPO check + species ID and the GBP 1,500 borehole (with plasticity + sulfate suites) buy the option on GBP 6-9k and must complete before the SE fixes the foundation design or the planning application shows the tree.
